clue.text: Heavenly bodies arrive the back way

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: going the back way means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word for a road is read from its end

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Some celestial objects approach from behind rather than head-on.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed street abbreviation ST becomes TS, tacked on after COME to make COMETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Comets are icy objects orbiting the sun, a kind of celestial body seen in the night sky.

clue.text: Too vain to give spontaneous applause

indicators.note: the words are made to give up a new word, rearranged rather than kept in order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An audience is too conceited to clap of its own accord.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of enthusiastic clapping from an audience, often a standing one.

clue.text: Come forth from the man at every opportunity

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the words that follow, a run of their letters

parts.note: a run spanning the end of the first word, two whole words and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone keeps popping out of a man's presence whenever the chance arises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opportunity' only completes the surface; the answer ends in the E of 'every'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, a formal synonym of come forth.

clue.text: Metal container in pig house is barely sufficient

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: a sty is where pigs are kept
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: A tin left in the pigsty is hardly enough to feed them.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer word comes first in the answer's order even though the clue names the container first; 'house' is a pig's home, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre or insufficient in amount, only just enough.

clue.text: Riches a natural source for a kind of treasurer

parts.note: surface reading: wealth is where a treasurer's work naturally begins
setter's reading: the word for riches is the natural source of this official's title, which is built on it

explanation.surface: Wealth is the obvious place a certain money-keeper gets started.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for ready money is the root of this job title; the rest of the clue just points at that. The printed clue may have lost a word, so this reading is tentative.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier handles the money in a bank, shop or business, a humble kind of treasurer.

clue.text: 'Le Duc Ingenu' needs bringing out, partly

indicators.note: only part of the quoted phrase is used, a run of its letters

parts.note: a run beginning at the second letter of the first word and ending inside the last

explanation.surface: A French title, The Innocent Duke, is in need of being published.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits between the hidden phrase and its indicator, which the solver may not expect.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or elicit something latent, so educing means drawing or bringing it out.

clue.text: Attempted to get about very quietly, and fell

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to have attempted is to have tried
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone tried to creep around silently and took a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Musical dynamics marks are a common source of letters: p is quietly, so pp is very quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripped means stumbled over something, and fell is used loosely for the same accident.

clue.text: Not so warm taking in an object for straining

indicators.note: something taking in another thing holds it inside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: less warm means colder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something cooler absorbs an object that is being strained, perhaps in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straining' suggests effort, but here it is the kitchen sense of draining liquid off food.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated kitchen bowl used to drain or strain food such as pasta.

clue.text: Male gets literary collection tomorrow in Barcelona

parts.note: a man is a male
ana is a collection of sayings or anecdotes about a person

explanation.surface: A man acquires an anthology, but only tomorrow, in true Spanish fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA is a crossword favourite: a gathering of someone's table talk or anecdotes, as in Johnsoniana.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is the Spanish word for tomorrow, and Barcelona places the word in Spain.

clue.text: Designed to warm stomach or head in bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a warming alcoholic drink taken before bed

definitions.note: short for something designed to warm the head in bed
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a soft cap once worn to keep the head warm while sleeping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed to warm' governs both halves: one thing warms the stomach, the other the head in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a bedtime drink of spirits and the old-fashioned woollen cap worn for sleeping.

clue.text: Five to four on the insect for French living

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
IV is the Roman numeral four
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Reads like betting odds of five to four on an insect, as if at a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five to four on' imitates racing odds, but the numbers are Roman numerals laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivant is the French present participle meaning living, familiar from bon vivant.

clue.text: Eggy part of lady's dress, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the yellow centre of an egg, which is pronounced the same as the dressmaking term

explanation.surface: Someone has spilt egg on part of a woman's frock, or so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: The L in the egg word is silent, so it and the dress term sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressmaking a yoke is the fitted panel across the shoulders or hips from which the rest of a garment hangs.

clue.text: Bridge partners ever poetically making a show of contempt

parts.note: South and North are partners at the bridge table
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A pair of card players are always scornful of their opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and N and S play as a pair against E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneer is to curl the lip and speak in a way that openly displays scorn.

clue.text: There's no noise since the French went in

definitions.note: a clause; the answer is the noun for the state it describes

indicators.note: something that went in is now inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: It has been quiet ever since the French troops marched in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' points to the French word for the, not to French people.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is the complete absence of sound, the state of affairs when no noise is heard.

clue.text: Pole coming up with mixed gin and" absconding romantically

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Polish man turns up with a gin cocktail while running off with his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray quotation mark is an artefact of the newspaper print.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping means running away secretly to marry, usually without parental consent.

clue.text: Fencing thrust to tear the toes, perhaps

parts.note: to rip is to tear

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word could be arranged otherwise, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fencer's lunge looks set to slash an opponent's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick return thrust made by a fencer after parrying an attack.

clue.text: Grow old in the way, showed great anger

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone stuck growing old in a rut finally lost their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE sits between the R and D of the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Raged is the past tense of rage, to be violently furious, which matches showing great anger.

clue.text: Caste is arranged and 99 becomes extremely austere

indicators.note: arranged means set out in some order, here a new order of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
IC is 99 in Roman numerals, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: A social order is reorganised and someone aged 99 turns very strict.
explanation.walkthrough: IC for 99 is a crossword shortcut, not a standard Roman form (which would be XCIX).
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic life is one of severe self-denial, rejecting comfort and pleasure.

clue.text: Herald takes me in and loses his head for a stone

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other
losing the head means dropping the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A messenger admits the speaker and is beheaded for a gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Herald without its H leaves ERALD, and ME slips in after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious gemstone, a variety of beryl.

clue.text: An article — get me it, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words could be some other arrangement, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper asks someone to fetch a particular thing for them.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article or object, as in an item on a list or for sale.

clue.text: She's disguised in smart hat and suit

indicators.note: something disguised in other words is concealed within them, a run of their letters

parts.note: a run spanning the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: A woman goes incognito dressed in a chic hat and suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' stands for any woman's name; 'and suit' just completes the outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha is a woman's name, so it can stand for the pronoun she as one example.

clue.text: In buildings they support, in feet they need it

definitions.note: a clause describing a plural noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: curved structures that carry weight over an opening

definitions.note: a clause describing a plural noun; 'it' is support
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the curved undersides of the feet, which can fall and need propping up

explanation.walkthrough: The word 'support' turns from verb to noun between the halves: building arches give it, fallen foot arches need it.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved load-bearing span over a doorway and the raised curve of the sole share one name.

clue.text: Could take mere ploy to make hirer of workers

indicators.note: to make something from materials is to form them into a new shape, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mere trick might be all it takes to become someone's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer is the person or firm that hires and pays staff to do work.

clue.text: Auburn, but ain't it funny

indicators.note: funny can mean odd or peculiar, so the letters are put into an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on reddish-brown hair with a chuckle: ain't it funny?
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is a bright reddish-brown colour, named for the Venetian painter who favoured such hair in his portraits.

clue.text: Path once designed to lead to the monument

indicators.note: something designed has been planned and laid out afresh, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A walkway was once laid out to lead visitors up to a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial honouring the dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, as at Whitehall in London.

clue.text: Sheltered shopping path in popular cadet college

indicators.note: the answer sits in the following words, spread across their letters

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A covered walkway of shops stands within a well-liked military academy.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcade is a covered passage lined with shops, sheltering shoppers from the weather.
